prs.title: Remove MessagePort's close event
prs.author: nicolo-ribaudo
prs.body:
As discussed in https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12957. Note that I have no interest in working on re-adding the event, but the commit description should have enough pointer for somebody else that might.

Closes https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10201, closes https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/12797, closes https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12957

Commit message:
> Remove MessagePort's close event
>
> This is a revert of cc2634fed12737f342da865f1f5c4f751c2da601 (it's not a "clean" revert because of some other changes that happened in the meantime).
>
> This means that this patch also restores the older GC semantics: a port is not easily GC-able, it is not exlicitly disentangled when the other half's owner document is destroyed, and relies on polling to see if the other half is still alive. I believe this matches Firefox's behavior, which is also what I believe the discussion in #10201 leads to.
>
> Note that browsers have all different GC semantics (according to Claude):
> - Chromium makes a port uncollectable only if it's already started
> - Firefox does not collect them
> - WebKit keeps the port uncollectable only if it has a message listener
>
> Given that no browser ships the `close` events this revert is probably the best thing to do; if somebody in the future wants to reintroduce it some relevant discussions are:
> - https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/1766
> - https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/9933
> - https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10201

prs.title: Split the scripting is disabled check for event handlers
prs.author: annevk
prs.body:
Moving this check to compile time in 1a249c2 restored the arrangement from
before 905b721 ([WebDriver BiDi] enable and disable scripting via BiDi) and
undid it: with scripting disabled through WebDriver BiDi an event handler IDL
attribute returned null again, and an event handler whose value is a function
ran.

"Scripting is disabled" bundles three conditions that want different treatment,
so check them where they belong instead:

* A null browsing context and the sandboxed scripts browsing context flag stop
  an internal raw uncompiled handler from being compiled. This is what
  implementations do, and it is all they do: an event handler IDL attribute set
  to a function still runs in a document without a browsing context, and in
  Chromium and Gecko in one sandboxed without allow-scripts.
* WebDriver BiDi scripting being disabled stops the event handler from running,
  while leaving the IDL attribute returning the function.

Tests: https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/62719 and
https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/56715

***

/cc @sadym-chromium @zcorpan — sorry, #12944 was mine and I did not notice it
was undoing the event handler part of #11441.

prs.title: Editorial: fix COOP argument, variable, and link mix-ups
prs.author: shannonbooth
prs.body: While implementing COOP, I ran into "enforce a response's opener policy" not passing "check if COOP values require a browsing context group switch" in an order that matches its declaration. Reviewing that fix with AI turned up a few more issues nearby, which this fixes too. Changes: - fix COOP group switch check argument order - fix undefined variable in report-only COOP check - fix type confusion in popup COOP check - fix link to access to another window COOP report - fix COOP access from an opened window report body Reporting integration seems to have some further problems (e.g github.com/whatwg/html/issues/8336, github.com/whatwg/html/issues/11365), but I've tried keeping this bit smaller. *** /browsers.html ( diff )

prs.title: COEP/COOP report-to takes endpoint name not URL (typo)
prs.author: hamishwillee
prs.body: The coep report-to section reports that the parameter takes a valid URL string. This uses the reporting API, in which report-to should take an endpoint name, as sent to the browser in the header [Reporting-Endpoints](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Reporting-Endpoints) - and mapping to a URL via that name. I am not sure this adequately meets your conventions sorry! Fixes #11365 *** /browsers.html ( diff ) /infrastructure.html ( diff )

prs.title: Editorial: move COOP access report endpoint checks
prs.author: annevk
prs.body: "Queue violation reports for accesses" started with steps that used coop, coopValue, and disposition, none of which it defines. Move the null reporting endpoint check into the "access to" report algorithms, as the "access from" ones already have it, and remove the rest. Also remove a stray comma nearby. This is a follow-up to aa347f36fd8738fc9d108b23ca5a32cde823c3fd. *** /browsers.html ( diff )

prs.title: Use DOM's node creation algorithms in the XML parser
prs.author: annevk
prs.body: The XML parser only said how to create elements, through create an element for a token, which always uses a null prefix. The other nodes it creates had no specified realm, and its processing instructions no attribute map, so getAttribute() returned null for them. Give create an element for a token an optional prefix and name a creation algorithm for each type of node, as 85f453b854574dd4541c9b4106783c887865fbf5 did for the HTML parser. ---- Skipping the template as the processing instruction behavior is already tested and I'm pretty sure the element behavior is too. *** /infrastructure.html ( diff ) /parsing.html ( diff ) /xhtml.html ( diff )
